clue.text: President Trump livid, in a rage

indicators.note: being in a rage implies wild disorder, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A news-style line reporting an American president losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to read 'President' as Trump himself, but he is only fodder: 'in a rage' is the anagram signal, and the letters of TRUMP LIVID IN A rearrange into another head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian leader holds the title of president of the Russian Federation.

clue.text: Fortunately, bravely — though not at first

indicators.note: the synonym for bravely is to lose its opening letter, as the start is not wanted

parts.note: to act pluckily is to act with courage, so bravely

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that a lucky outcome came about through good fortune rather than courage, at least initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' removes the P from PLUCKILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are sentence adverbs meaning 'as luck would have it', so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Head supporting action by which to obtain a new name

definitions.text: by which to obtain a new name

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece placed underneath holds the other up, so the head word goes below the action word

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax counted per head

explanation.surface: It reads like a remark about a manager backing an action taken to rebrand something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' works because this is a down entry: the head word sits underneath, holding the action up. 'Head' is an old sense, as in a poll tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is the British legal document a person signs to change their name officially.

clue.text: Pence perhaps beginning to madden former President

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word gives its opening letter only

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, US President in the 1950s

explanation.surface: Vice-President Pence seemingly starting to infuriate an ex-President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pence' is not money here but the US politician, whose first name is the answer; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The US vice-president surnamed Pence has this as his first name, so he is an example of someone so called.

clue.text: Near mosque, oddly, as are some early churches

indicators.note: something arranged oddly is out of its usual order, so the letters before it are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A remark that some old churches, strangely, stand next to a mosque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a comment on the setting but signals the anagram of NEAR MOSQUE; it does not pick odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the round-arched architectural style of the 11th and 12th centuries, used in many early medieval churches.

clue.text: One opens doors for Montmartre pawnbroker

parts.note: un is the French for one, and Montmartre is a district of Paris
clé is the French word for a key, the thing that opens doors

explanation.surface: A Parisian pawnbroker seemingly acting as a doorman in Montmartre.
explanation.walkthrough: Montmartre, a district of Paris, tells you both pieces are French. 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: In old slang a pawnbroker was called by this family title, from pawned goods being 'at my relative's'.

clue.text: Isn't it commonly showcasing adult Yankee senselessness?

indicators.note: to showcase something is to hold it on display, so the slang word contains the next piece

parts.note: innit is the casual British contraction of isn't it
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question asking whether an American's foolishness is plain to see, phrased in street slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innit' is British street slang for 'isn't it'; 'showcasing' puts A inside it, and Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe silliness or a lack of sense, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: 27's predecessor arranged loan rollover

indicators.note: rolling something over turns it about, so these letters are tumbled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A financial line about a loan being rolled over by arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rollover' looks like finance jargon but is the anagram signal; 'arranged' is fodder, not the indicator. 27 across is the first President Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: George H. W. Bush took office in 1989 directly after this actor-turned-president.

clue.text: Unleaded pinchbeck kept in a controlled environment

indicators.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead, so lead-free means those two letters are removed from the word that follows

explanation.surface: Cheap imitation gold, free of lead, stored under controlled conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinchbeck is a cheap gold-coloured alloy. 'Unleaded' removes PB, the chemical symbol for lead, from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under control or restrained is said to be held so, as with an illness kept from spreading.

clue.text: President Mao angered, having been done

indicators.note: an angered person is stirred up, so the letters of the preceding words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Chairman Mao enraged at having been cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' here means mimicked, as in 'he did a great Mao'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is informal for mimicking them, as an impressionist does.

clue.text: Acme Co working to introduce new construction project

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something into the middle, so the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
working implies the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm called Acme Co bringing in a new building scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ACME CO to MECCAO, and 'to introduce' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal strips-and-bolts kit is a children's construction toy for building models.

clue.text: Smarten up pages around the margin

indicators.note: the abbreviation for pages is placed around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a rim is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: An editor's instruction to tidy the edges of some pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen or groom oneself is to make one's appearance neater, which is what smartening up means.

clue.text: Frau Merkel's current carbon storage plant?

indicators.note: her name holds the following letters as a store holds goods

parts.note: Angela Merkel was the German chancellor
I is the symbol for electric current
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A question about the German chancellor's carbon storage plant, as if an energy scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storage' places I and C inside ANGELA. 'plant' is the misleading word: a herb, not a facility.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic herb, whose candied stems decorate cakes, is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Tired-looking writer of nonsense in Times I had reportedly contracted

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in four by six
Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the following piece is taken by its sound
contracted tells you the two words are squeezed into their short apostrophe form

parts.note: I had, shortened, is written I'd

explanation.surface: A confession of having caught something, set in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'contracted' shortens I had to its apostrophe form, and 'reportedly' says that short form is taken by sound. Times means multiplied, as in four by six.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with bleary eyes has a blurred, sleepy look, so seems tired.

clue.text: Generous hand bringing colour to Her Majesty's cheeks?

definitions.meaning: a hand of cards that gives its holder the best possible deal

definitions.text: bringing colour to Her Majesty's cheeks?
definitions.meaning: a regal blush, the monarch's face reddening

explanation.walkthrough: In poker the ace-high straight in one suit beats everything; the second reading is a royal blush.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ace-to-ten run in one suit is the strongest possible hand, a lavish deal of cards.

clue.text: He wrote notes alongside river delta

parts.note: by means beside or alongside
R is the map abbreviation for river
Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone jotting down notes beside a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English Tudor composer; 'notes' are musical, not written jottings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor composer wrote music, that is, notes on a staff.

clue.text: Such as Little Boy Blue broadcast, with catastrophic results?

definitions.text: Such as Little Boy Blue broadcast, with catastrophic results?

parts.words: Such as Little Boy Blue broadcast, with catastrophic results?
parts.note: Little Boy was the weapon dropped on Hiroshima; the nursery rhyme's Little Boy Blue blows his horn, and this device blew things apart across a wide area

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme character's radio appearance going disastrously wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme is a decoy: Little Boy was the codename of the weapon dropped on Hiroshima in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Boy was a nuclear fission device, a weapon of exactly this type.

clue.text: Damn … it's Yoko on the phone

indicators.note: a voice heard on the phone is only heard, so the surname is taken by how it is said

parts.note: Yoko Ono, the artist married to John Lennon

explanation.surface: Someone groaning on realising Yoko is calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link; the surname Ono said out loud gives the two-word exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of dismay when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Area north of Houston St a "lost cause"

parts.note: NoHo is the Manhattan neighbourhood named for lying north of Houston Street
per means a or each, as in ten pounds per hour

explanation.surface: A sign or remark dismissing a New York neighbourhood as hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: NoHo, like SoHo, is a Manhattan district named from its position relative to Houston Street. 'a' gives PER as in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no chance of success is a hopeless case, a lost cause.

clue.text: Rail: Labour rejected American deal

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party
trade means to deal in goods

explanation.surface: A headline: a Labour Party rail policy rejecting an American trade deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like trains but means a handrail; 'rejected' is the reversal signal on the party abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of posts topped by a handrail on a staircase or balcony forms a rail.

clue.text: Unpopular, but usually accommodating growth

indicators.note: the words accommodate, or hold within them, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Remark that something unpopular nonetheless tends to make room for expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth' looks economic but means a plant: the strawberry tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree is a shrub, and a plant is loosely a growth.

clue.text: Camels graveyards?

parts.note: Camel is a cigarette brand, and the place spent cigarettes end up is the container for butts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Camels' is not the animal but the cigarette brand; the place where they die is the dish for stubbed-out cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent cigarettes are stubbed out and left in these dishes, a final resting place for smokes.

clue.text: Criticises prices

definitions.meaning: to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means charges or tariffs, and the verb, archaically, means scolds.

clue.text: Top criminal Russian fighter accepting bribe on a regular basis

indicators.note: the jet takes the letters into itself

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one of the word

explanation.surface: A crime boss who takes regular bribes from a Russian pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes the even letters of bribe, R and B, which go inside MIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for the boss of a criminal gang, the head villain.

clue.text: Examine Charlie in hospital

indicators.note: the letter goes in the word for hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A doctor checking on a patient named Charlie in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over closely is to scrutinise, which is what examine means.

clue.text: Pay them off in compassion

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paying someone off out of sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean sharing in another's feelings or suffering.

clue.text: Some toast Tory admitting defeat

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a rout is a heavy defeat

explanation.surface: A Tory toasting the party while conceding a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' looks like a raised glass but is the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small cubes of fried or toasted bread served in soup.

clue.text: Quietly live next to Tina Turner's city, ignoring an upper-class George

indicators.note: next to places one piece beside the next

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to reside is to live somewhere

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Nutbush, Tennessee, is Tina Turner's hometown, from her song Nutbush City Limits
U is the abbreviation for upper-class

explanation.surface: A quiet life near a singer's hometown, minus the posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes U from NUTBUSH, leaving NTBUSH. George here is either President Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Both US Presidents named Bush had George as a first name.
